thread:
Maria - CustSuccess: Hey team, just escalated a live customer report — their Dedicated pool p95/p99 jumped ~3-4x starting ~09:10 UTC, and a bunch of requests hit timeouts. They saw scale events but instances were slow to route.
Samir - Oncall: @Maria thanks — customer name? logs?
Maria - CustSuccess: Customer: AcmeData (large batch scoring). I grabbed a snippet from their app logs and our proxy: 
```
2026-03-15T09:09:58Z ERROR request id=... downstream timeout after 30s
2026-03-15T09:10:02Z WARN autoscaler: scale_up event triggered for pool Dedicated-ACME-1 desired=12 current=6
2026-03-15T09:10:14Z INFO provisioning: new gpu instance booting id=gpu-az3-77
2026-03-15T09:10:58Z INFO routing: no warm instance available, queued=48
```
Maria - CustSuccess: They say the SDK retries but latency kills their SLA. They also attached a recording of >10s cold starts.
Alyssa - SRE: Oof. Any metrics from the pool? memory/queue length/queue wait times?
Samir - Oncall: Pushing grafana panel now.
autoscale-bot: [alert] pool Dedicated-ACME-1 queued_requests > 30 for 420s. scaling_in_progress=true
Samir - Oncall: Snapshot from 09:08-09:16: CPU fine, GPU utilization low (because instances are still booting), queue wait percentiles: p50=200ms p95=6.2s p99=12.8s. Provisioning lag (time from scale event to ready) avg=46s median=38s.
Jon - PlatformEng: That's the provisioning lag we measured in last stress test, but 46s is higher than expected. Which cloud? AZ?
Maria - CustSuccess: GCP us-west3, zone c. Customer said they scaled from 6->12.
Alyssa - SRE: Two hypotheses: (1) VM boot time spike in that zone (cloud issue) (2) our attach/startup hook is blocking longer (model loading/quantization step)
Samir - Oncall: I pulled host logs on one of the slow instances: 
```
[09:10:15] containerd: pulling image redwood/infer:vm-rt-1.3
[09:10:22] runtime: loading model shard 0 (L2 cache miss)
[09:10:41] runtime: performing quantize fallback for layer 27
[09:10:55] runtime: ready and accepting connections
```
Samir - Oncall: model shard load + quantize fallback ~20s. Quantize fallback happens when cached quant kernel not present for this instance type.
Jon - PlatformEng: That suggests kernel selection path falls back to slower code path. Did we recently roll a kernel package? Any images updated in the last 48h?
Alyssa - SRE: I checked image tag — no image roll in that pool since last week. But we did push a kernel build to the artifact repo; only newer hosts pick it up. Could be a mismatch between prebuilt kernels and instance type.
Maria - CustSuccess: Customer is asking for immediate mitigations — what can we do right now?
Alyssa - SRE: Short-term mitigations: (a) increase min_replicas to avoid cold starts during their big batch (b) enable pre-warm: create warm standby instances in the pool (c) route heavy traffic to Hosted fallback if possible (d) bump autoscale cooldown to avoid thundering scale events.
Samir - Oncall: I've temporarily set min_replicas=10 on Dedicated-ACME-1 and increased autoscale.max_burst to +4. Also set cooldown to 90s from 30s. Monitoring now.
Jon - PlatformEng: Good. For medium-term: we need to ensure model artifacts and kernel packages are preinstalled in our images for that instance family, or ship a fast quant kernel. Also improve our warmup hook to parallelize shard loading.
Maria - CustSuccess: Customer asked for repro steps so they can test. What should I give them?
Alyssa - SRE: Repro steps for them: send a burst workload equivalent to N concurrent streams (their qps * concurrency) that would push queued_requests > 30 for >2 mins. Use the SDK with no retries and measure 95/99. Also capture logs from request header x-rid and the time trace.
Samir - Oncall: Added a lightweight endpoint /health/warm that forces a model load and responds after shard load completes — they can hit that during rollout to keep instances warm. I can expose it to them temporarily.
Jon - PlatformEng: For prevention: implement proactive scaling policy that predicts batch windows from historical signals and spins up earlier, and a warm pool that is always at least N% of max. Also push a kernel packaging fix to CI so new instances use optimized kernels.
Maria - CustSuccess: Customer appreciates the quick response. They're asking for remediation ETA and whether this will recur.
Alyssa - SRE: ETA for immediate remediation (min_replicas/cooldown/burst) — 10-15m to take effect. ETA for kernel fix + image bake — 48-72h. ETA for proactive predictor + warm pool feature — 2-3 sprints.
Samir - Oncall: Monitoring update: queued_requests dropped from 48->6 after min_replicas change, p95 down to 800ms, p99 ~1.6s. Customer confirmed fewer errors.
Maria - CustSuccess: I'll relay those numbers. They want postmortem and suggested guardrails to avoid surprises.
Jon - PlatformEng: I'll own a short postmortem doc: root cause: slow model shard/kernel selection during provisioning in GCP us-west3c causing provisioning lag -> queued requests -> p95/p99 spikes. Remediations: patch kernel packaging, add warm pool, expose warm endpoint, proactive scaling, and a playbook to raise min_replicas for scheduled large jobs.
Alyssa - SRE: Also add a fallback routing rule: if provisioning lag > X and queued > Y, route batches to hosted compatible model to preserve SLA.
Samir - Oncall: Leaving notes in the incident channel and will follow up with cloud provider for any underlying host slow boots.
Maria - CustSuccess: Thanks all. I'll schedule a customer follow-up in 30m and share the mitigation timeline. :thumbsup:
Jon - PlatformEng: Leaving a TODO: add synthetic canary test that simulates cold-shard loads to catch regressions in model startup time.
Alyssa - SRE: Agreed. Adding to backlog.
autoscale-bot: [resolved] alert Dedicated-ACME-1 queued_requests back to normal
Samir - Oncall: Closing thread for now, will reopen if numbers regress.
